principles: Use the existing gate-consumed evaluator instead of a parallel policy path.
Fail closed on missing, stale, or self-claimed review evidence.
Keep local Non-authority evidence visibly separate from Authority Server receipts.
Scope the change to real correctness gaps and avoid arbitrary workflow expansion.
drivers: DONE must block material code diffs with zero current-material review assurance.
Failure signals must make 3x1 local review sticky without confusing it with 3x2 independence.
Machine.canFinish and done-oracle output must remain logically consistent.

options.name: A: Extend existing review escalation evaluator into a review assurance evaluator
pros: Reuses the DONE checklist and canFinish consumer already wired to evaluateReviewEscalation
Minimizes new command and artifact surface
Keeps existing host verdict material/session/key binding semantics
cons: Requires careful naming/output updates because the old evaluator name says escalation even when enforcing the floor

options.name: B: Add a separate review_assurance_floor evaluator and DONE row
pros: Cleaner conceptual naming for the new floor
cons: Creates two review gates with overlapping host verdict logic
Raises risk of canFinish and done-oracle divergence

options.name: C: Force all code-changing stories through existing 3x2 escalation
pros: Can reuse current full quorum behavior directly
cons: Contradicts the accepted policy non-goal and overblocks ordinary clean code changes
Consumes more tokens without a failure signal

chosen: A: Extend existing review escalation evaluator into a review assurance evaluator
rationale: Option A fixes the actual correctness gap by extending the existing gate-consumed path, while preserving current 3x2 escalation semantics and the local Non-authority boundary.

preMortem.scenario: Docs-only tasks are overblocked as code diffs
preMortem.trigger: Diff classification treats any docs/requirements change as material code
preMortem.consequence: Low-risk typo or annotation stories pay unnecessary review cost and contradict the policy
preMortem.mitigation: Classify material code by source/runtime/test/script paths and explicitly exclude docs/markdown-only changes unless stronger high-risk policy already applies

preMortem.scenario: Local 3x1 is reported as Authority completion
preMortem.trigger: Status output or summary reuses authority/multiHost wording for local host verdicts
preMortem.consequence: The CLI overclaims production readiness and violates host-neutral Authority semantics
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authorityDone/fullAuthorityDone/productionDone false in reports and tests, and label 3x1 as degraded-single-host

preMortem.scenario: DONE checklist and machine guard diverge
preMortem.trigger: Only done-oracle rows are updated while canFinish still reads old evaluateReviewEscalation semantics
preMortem.consequence: session_brief or story_advance can disagree about whether DONE is allowed
preMortem.mitigation: Keep both consumers on one evaluator and add smoke coverage for failure/pass outcomes

preMortem.trigger: Evaluator only checks current open bugs/findings and forgets earlier validation failure or review finding events
preMortem.consequence: A story can fail, repair, and close with only one review despite the approved policy
preMortem.mitigation: Derive sticky signals from durable story artifacts/process events where available and add synthetic smoke cases for validation fail, bug, and verified finding
